scope: Jetson Xavier NX + ZCU102 fixed-point token selector break-even model (model only; no GPU, no board, no network, no measurement claims)

baseline_confusion_fix.superseded: the v1 J_ONLY baseline, which already included the Jetson software selector and the K-token post-B1 vision, so J_F_J shared that vision with the baseline and a post-B1 saving could not offset the FPGA round trip; and the v1 dense comparison, for which score generation was treated as cancelling
baseline_confusion_fix.fix: split the baseline into J_DENSE (no score, no selector, dense post-B1 vision) and J_PRUNED (Jetson score + software selector + K-token post-B1 vision) and report two strictly separated requirement sets, A algorithm benefit vs J_DENSE and B deployment choice vs J_PRUNED
baseline_confusion_fix.consequence: J_F_J vs J_PRUNED contains no vision saving term at all (T_vision_pruned cancels exactly); J_F_J vs J_DENSE keeps the T_score symbolic term; no full break-even in milliseconds relative to the old J_ONLY may be quoted

byte_contract.input_tokens: int8[G,4,1024] = G*4096 B (G dense groups, each 4 merge tokens of 1024 features)
byte_contract.input_score: uint16[G] = G*2 B (unsigned Q0.15 combined score produced on the Jetson; not generated inside the selector IP)
byte_contract.output_layout: 5 segments (tokens_int8 K*4096 B + group_index_uint16 + source_type_uint8 + region_id_uint8 + valid_uint8), each segment 64 B aligned, total 64 B aligned

reused: decimal serialization_ms convention (bytes*8/(gbps*1e9*eff)) and zero-overlap serialization lower bound
link + fixed-overhead sensitivity parameter style, and the 'sensitivity input, not a measurement' boundary
frozen 5-segment 64 B-aligned byte contract and the packed int8[G,4,1024] token grouping
not_inherited: the 2026-09-10 EXTERNAL_SELECTOR_ROUND_TRIP_REJECT verdict: it predates the fixed-point selector byte contract and the v4 csynth/cosim/OOC cycle evidence, used A6000 BF16 development-oracle stage timings, and assumed zero fixed link overhead; it is a stale conclusion, not a reused definition
the old cut-point oracle stage medians, which are not Jetson Xavier NX measurements
left_untouched: all selector RTL/HLS sources and the frozen golden reference

selector_evidence.evidence_note: selector cycle counts are read from the v4 csynth/cosim artifacts at model run time, never hand-filled; cosim verifies function only, OOC route WNS +0.689 ns at 5.000 ns is the timing evidence for the 200 MHz conversion, and neither is a full-system or on-board measurement

score_generation.note: Wt/Wv score generation stays on the Jetson; it is absent from J_DENSE, present in J_PRUNED/J_F_J/J_F_CONTINUE, and therefore does NOT cancel against the dense baseline; it cancels only in J_F_J vs J_PRUNED

T_score.definition: Wt/Wv score generation for the dense B1 groups

T_sel_sw.definition: software token selector on the Jetson

T_vision_dense.definition: dense post-B1 vision on the Jetson

T_vision_pruned.definition: K-token post-B1 vision on the Jetson; identical in J_PRUNED and J_F_J

T_fpga_downstream.definition: real FPGA downstream core after the selector

symbol_legend.T_vision_dense: dense post-B1 Jetson vision; total latency of J_DENSE
symbol_legend.T_vision_pruned: K-token post-B1 Jetson vision; identical in J_PRUNED and J_F_J
symbol_legend.T_score: Jetson Wt/Wv score generation; absent from J_DENSE
symbol_legend.T_sel_sw: Jetson software selector; present only in J_PRUNED
symbol_legend.T_link_dense(G): one-way serialization of the dense G-group send (G*4096 + G*2 bytes)
symbol_legend.T_link_return(K): one-way serialization of the selected K-token return (5-segment 64 B-aligned layout)
symbol_legend.F: one fixed software+DMA overhead per link leg
symbol_legend.S_prune: T_vision_dense - T_vision_pruned (Jetson post-B1 vision saved by pruning)

J_DENSE.description: no score, no selector; dense post-B1 vision on the Jetson
J_DENSE.baseline_role: dense algorithm baseline for comparison A

J_PRUNED.description: Jetson score + software selector + K-token post-B1 vision on the Jetson
J_PRUNED.baseline_role: pruned deployment baseline for comparison B and candidate for comparison A

J_F_J.description: Jetson score + FPGA selector round trip + the same K-token Jetson post-B1 vision
J_F_J.baseline_role: offload candidate; its K-token vision cancels exactly against J_PRUNED

J_F_CONTINUE.description: Jetson score + send to FPGA selector + real FPGA downstream core; no return to the Jetson
J_F_CONTINUE.baseline_role: offload candidate; requires a real FPGA downstream core

comparison_A_algorithm_vs_J_DENSE.question: does pruning or the heterogeneous selector beat dense post-B1 vision on the Jetson?

J_F_CONTINUE.requirement: T_vision_dense - T_fpga_downstream > T_score + T_link_dense + T_sel_fpga + F

comparison_B_deployment_vs_J_PRUNED.question: given that pruning is already the deployment, does moving the selector to the FPGA help?

J_F_CONTINUE.requirement: T_sel_sw + T_vision_pruned > T_link_dense + T_sel_fpga + F + T_fpga_downstream

break_even_definition.note: no full break-even in milliseconds is reported while T_score, T_sel_sw, T_vision_dense, T_vision_pruned and T_fpga_downstream are unmeasured; the tables report only the communication + FPGA-selector known part and state the remaining terms symbolically
break_even_definition.J_F_CONTINUE_vs_J_DENSE: T_vision_dense - T_fpga_downstream > T_score + T_link_dense + T_sel_fpga + F
break_even_definition.J_F_CONTINUE_vs_J_PRUNED: T_sel_sw + T_vision_pruned > T_link_dense + T_sel_fpga + F + T_fpga_downstream

link_profiles.model: one-way pure serialization time = bytes / (throughput_MBps * 1000); each link leg that is used additionally carries exactly one fixed software+DMA overhead, no overlap with compute
link_profiles.note: parameter scan only; these are not Xavier/ZCU102 measurements

warnings: No GPU was used, no ZCU102 access, no board measurements, no network.
This is a parameterized requirement model, not a measured Jetson Xavier NX result.
T_score, T_sel_sw, T_vision_dense, T_vision_pruned and T_fpga_downstream are unmeasured; only the communication + FPGA-selector part is numeric.
The reported millisecond values are lower bounds on the required term and must be quoted together with '+T_score' or 'T_sel_sw must exceed X', never as a full break-even.
The selector cycle counts come from v4 csynth (pre-route static bound) and functional C/RTL cosim; cosim does not prove 200 MHz.
The 200 MHz conversion is supported only by the separate OOC place-and-route timing report (WNS +0.689 ns at 5.000 ns), not by an on-board clock measurement.
Effective throughput and fixed software+DMA overhead are scanned assumptions, not measurements.
